title: Choosing an Olds Recording trumpet in return for his endorsement
summary: At the factory he was handed papers and picked an Olds Recording trumpet over a Mendez model; Wilson reads the endorsement letter for U.S. Customs.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Cornet or trumpet: choosing and owning horns

blocks.x: He hasn't said anything, so far.

So when we get out, and I go around with Vic, and Vic try out, oh half a dozens of horns were in this there, and beautiful factory, and all over these beautiful horns, all that stuff. And Vic would play this one. How would you like to have this ? So, finally, we decided on -- I said I like the sound of that one better.

So, Vic said I think so too. Anyway, now we went and -- (Laughs) -- went in there so the gentleman who worked there, he said okay, now I want to show you some. I said well, I'm visiting. You didn't tell me -- he said aw, well take a look at it. I said well all right (Laughs).

So I took a look at the horns, and here he went in the office and went through the business, and he kept -- the manager kept looking at me. He says Herman, what am I going to do with you? I said I don't know. I said well, should he make me an offer, save me a few bucks, I will buy me a horn, maybe. You know.
So -- so he pulled out two or three long papers there, and he says sign here, sign that one, and sign here and sign this, says go out and pick out a horn.
So I went there, and Vic was with me,
and I pick, pick, pick, pick, and I got -- I picked this one. So --
Yeah. So he wanted me to take a much better horn, a Mendez model. You know Mendez's?
Uh-huh. Ohhhh! It was beautiful. I have a recording of his. But I -- I didn't like it. The bell was more like a hammered brass, or -- and it cost much more money than this.
This is the -- in the bell. It's in the bell.
: I see, I see it right here, but I'm trying to decipher it. R-e-c-o-r-d -- Recording.
: Recording, made -- yeah, made by Olds.
Uh-huh. And I don't know, I seem to like this. I like it much better, and it looked like a sort of a damn fool, but I -- that's what I liked, and what I wanted. So --
So I got it. And later on I tried to change my mind, I think, but I was too late.
Oh, you decided you would have liked something else better?
Yes, mainly because it's a better horn. I mean it's got the -- could have gotten the better horn.
Oh, I see, so you get it -- you endorse the --
Well what's -- yeah, this is -- well, this says Turner Musical Instruments, Limited. That's the Canadian thing for Olds?
-- you know, so in case I --
What Herman has given me is a letter from Turner Musical Instruments, Limited addressed to Whom it May Concern, U. S. Customs.

Saying that this will confirm that Turner Musical Instruments, Limited has presented Mr. Herman Autrey with a new instrument, Olds R-10 Recording Trumpet 579992 in return for his artist's endorsement of our product. Mr. Autrey has provided us with a signed publicity and promotional release which allows us to use his picture and endorsement in our advertising. And it's signed by A. A. Betts, vice-president.
